STANDARD: The Healthcare Organisation ensures patients are provided with safe, high- quality inpatient and outpatient care throughout the care delivery process. They should do this from the time that the patient enters the healthcare organisation or service through to when the patient is discharged or transferred to another health facility-service; and during any ongoing care they provide after discharge.
The Healthcare Organisation should implement evidence-based practice and a have a process for assessing the appropriateness and effectiveness of care and services, and the settings they are delivered in.
Standard 17 National Health Service Standards (NHSS) Vol. 2 (2nd Edition) National Quality Standard

The Operating Theatre Services have combined multidisciplinary healthcare personnel, e.g. surgeons, anaesthetists, nurses, theatre technician and other support staff in delivering a high standard of comprehensive patient care to those who require operative procedures during their stay in the Facility.

The Vision, Mission of the Facility are accessible. The Goals of the Operating Theatre Services suit its scope and are clearly documented. It should reflect the aspirations of the service and the needs of the community.
The Mission, Vision and Goals of the Organisation are visible, endorsed and dated.
There is an endorsed and dated department Organisational chart with lines of functions and reporting relationships.
Relevant policies are available in the department. (National Health Plan, National Health Service Standards, etc.).
Evidence of submission of an Annual Implementation Plan and budget.
Evidence of fee structure (if fees are collected).

There is a mechanism to ensure effective interaction between the Head of the Services or the Officer in Charge (OIC) and the Organisation’s Governing Body and Senior Management. The Head of Services shall also be involved for the following aspects of management of the services;
Preparation of budget and ensuring that expenditure remains within the budget allocated
Human resource
Facility and equipment management
Safety and performance improvement activities and risk management
Letter of appointment and terms of reference as the Head of Service.
Letter of appointment and terms of reference of the Head of Service in other hospital committees.
Evidence of (a) to (d) in meeting minutes/correspondence indicating the involvement of the Head of Service.
Request for allocation for budget and staffing.

Regular staff meetings are held between Head of Service and staff with sufficient regularity to discuss issues pertaining to the Operating Theatre Services. These meetings are minuted and communicated to all staff.
Meeting minutes are available, disseminated and acknowledged by staff.
There is sufficient attendance for the meetings with adequate representatives of the service.
Frequency of meetings are as scheduled.
Discussions and resolutions are implemented. (problems not solved are brought forward to the next meeting till resolved).

Appropriate statistics and records are maintained in the department in and used for managing services and patient care. The following (among others) are available;
Workload/census for types of OT and nature of cases.
Quarterly and annual report
Incident reports and register
Staffing number and staff profile
Staff training records
Data on performance improvement
Intensive Care workload such as number of admissions, bed occupancy rate, ventilator days, average length of stay
The statistics and records from (a) to (h) are available.
The NHSS Toolkit Assessment (checklist) for the relevant level has been completed in the past 6 months.
There is a list of services provided to other Units in the Facility.
Documented list of services provided to other Units in the Facility by the Operating Theatre Services
Records (a) to (e) are maintained in the OT.

Verification of the following by on-site inspection;
Filled consent taking form.
Specimen book for lab investigations.
Anaesthetic and drug records
Register of all operations done in the OT.
Documentation on disposal of dangerous drugs.
Patient medical records in details of procedure and surgeon and personnel involved.
Documented evidence of the counting of accountable (e.g. gauze, instruments etc) items used and a copy of the record is included in the patient's medical record.
Swab count and instrument count record are in patient records.
Support services such as radiology, pathology, and blood bank are available. Effective communication and relationships with these services are maintained.
Cross departmental policies regarding the related support services are available.
Evidence of compliance to such policies are observed on-site.

The Operating Theatre Services shall be directed by a qualified and competent medical practitioner, and staffed by suitably qualified and competent clinical staff to achieve the goals and objectives of the Services. There are sufficient staffing levels, a staff supervision structure, performance appraisals and ongoing commitment to continuing medical education.

The are written and dated job descriptions for each category of staff that include:
Qualification, training and experience for the position
Lines of authority
Accountability, functions and responsibilities
Reviewed when required if there is major change in job scope 
Statutory regulations
Administrative and clinical job scope
There are records of credentials of Head of Services.
There are dated and specific job descriptions for each staff that include (a) to (f).
The job description is acknowledged by the staff and signed by the Head of Service and dated.
The scope of work in the job description aligns with the training, skill and experience of the staff (credentialling)
The Operating Theatre Services Nurse Manager has a postgraduate training in peri-operative nursing and has management skills.
Letter of appointment of the Operating Services Nurse Manager.
Credentials of the OT Nurse Manager.
All staff holds current registration with the relevant professional body.
Evidence of current registration for all cadres of staff (annual practicing certificate).
The staff works within their job description and job scope.
Observation that cadres of staff are working according to their job description and job scope.

There are continuing education activities for staff to pursue professional interests and to prepare for current and future changes in practice. This should include;
New surgical, anaesthetic and OT procedures
Regular fire and evacuation drills
Resuscitation techniques
Use of new equipment in surgical operations and its maintenance and calibration
Infection prevention and control
Training calendar includes in-house/ external courses/ workshops/ conferences.
Training for each staff including training in life support is kept in the Department.
There are ongoing Continuous Professional Activities in the Department.
The educational needs of staff are addressed following findings from incidents reports, mortality audits and performance improvement studies.
Evidence of staff training because of recommendations made from incident reports or mortality and morbidity reviews.

In a Facility where undergraduate medical, nursing and allied health training programmes are conducted, the Facility shall ensure there are sufficient skilled trained staff to provide clinical supervision of students.
Evidence of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
Staff including medical practitioners receive evaluation of their performance at the completion of the probationary period and annually thereafter, or as defined by the Organisation.
Performance appraisal for staff including medical practitioners is completed upon probationary period and as an annual exercise.
Where appropriate, the Facility shall endeavour to undertake clinical research using available resources.
Documented evidence of research activities in the Department.
Enough personnel and support staff with appropriate qualifications are employed to enable the services to meet the need of the services.
Number of staff and qualification should commensurate with workload.
There should be one anaesthetic scientific officer per OT.
There should be one perioperative postgraduate nurse per OT.
In the recovery area, there should be 1 qualified nurse to 3 patients.

There is a structured orientation programme for all newly appointed staff to the Operating Theatre Services including medical practitioners and for those new to specific areas that include the following;
Explanation of the goals, objectives, policies and procedures of the Facility and those of the Operating Theatre Services.
Lines of authority and areas of responsibility. 
Explanation of duties and functions.
Explanation of the methods of assigning clinical care and the standards of clinical practice. 
Handover communication.
Processes for resolving practice/ethical dilemmas in a timely manner.
Information about safety procedures. 
Training in basic/advanced life support techniques.
Methods of obtaining appropriate resource materials.
Staff appraisal procedures for the Operating Theatre services
Education on Patient and Family Rights
Evidence of policy stating that all staff have to attend a structured orientation programme.
Attendance list of those having attended the orientation programme.

There are written and dated policies for all activities of the Operating Theatre Services. These policies reflect current standards of medical practice, relevant regulations and statutory requirements. These policies and procedures, terms of reference, by laws, rules and regulations state how the clinical staff regulate themselves and provide patient care.
There are written policies and procedures for the Operating Theatre Services which are consistent with the overall policies of the Facility, regulatory requirements and current standard practices.
Evidence of documented policies and procedures for the service.
The policies and procedures are endorsed and dated.
There is a periodic review at least once in three years.
Copies of policies, by laws, regulations and relevant acts are accessible on site for staff reference
Policies and procedures are developed by a committee in collaboration with staff and with other departments if needed.
Minutes of committee meetings on development and revision on policies and procedures.

The policies and procedures documentation shall address at least the following topics;
Description of the organisational structure of the OT Services
The use of updated Standard Treatment Guidelines.
Handover communication
Drug prescription, dispensing and administration
Blood transfusion 
Incident reports 
Infection Prevention and Control, including aseptic procedures, terminal cleaning and procedures for infectious patients
Informed consent
Handling and disposal of sharps
Prevention of anaesthetic equipment hazards
Maintenance of scavenging equipment for removal of various vapours and anaesthetic gases
Patient identification, with the nature and site of the operation marked and verified by the surgeon and the consent documents checked
Counting procedures for accountable items including the procedures to be adopted in the event of incorrect counts
Patient management during recovery from anaesthesia and surgery
The role of the OT Services in the fire and disaster plans of the Facility
Priorities in the use of OT time and space
"Group Cross Match" and "Screen and hold" policy for blood transfusion practices for patients undergoing surgery 
Clear communication lines for obtaining emergency blood and blood products for cases of unexpected haemorrhage. 
Clear written policies and procedure for the involvement of vendor in providing specialized equipment/consumables for patient care in the OT where applicable
Documented policies and procedures that address (a) to (s).
Staff are briefed on the policies and procedures (meeting minutes or circulation acknowledgement).
The service shall operate on a 24-hour basis providing level of care appropriate to the facility.
Staffing level reflects a good mix of senior and junior staff.
On call roster is dated and authorised.

The Head of Operating Theatre Services shall ensure adequate facilities and equipment that are safe and appropriate are available for the staff to function effectively and to meet the goals and objectives of the Services.
The design and layout of the Operating Theatre provides adequate space and includes features listed in (a) to (i).

The design of the Operating Suite Services supports efficient systems for the management of perioperative services which include;
Operating rooms are treated as "clean" rooms.
Fire alarm and fire-fighting equipment and appropriate sign posting.
Ventilation system should provide positive pressure from the cleanest areas to less clean area 
Definitive traffic flow patterns and demarcation of sterile and non-sterile zones.
Ready access for routing emergency patients  
Free movement of patient trolleys throughout the suite with a minimum of cross traffic. 
Reception of the patient near the junction of sterile and non-sterile zones (air-lock zone); 
Uninterrupted power supply (UPS) system in operating theatres shall be provided with an alarm system at the reception counter which will be triggered when the system is not charged. 
The medical gas system in the operating theatres shall be monitored to ensure that it is functioning. 
Colour coding for electrical outlets shall be according to international standards.
Design and layout of the Operating Theatre with features (a) to (j).
Verification of appropriateness of design of the OT by inspection.
Log book on medical gas monitoring.

Perioperative services must have the following systems;
Adequate numbers of general power outlets distributed according to needs of each area.
Adequate provision for emergency power outlets for lighting and suction of an appropriate nature.
Suitable lighting. 
Adequate medical gas and suction supplies 
A means of environmental control of temperature and humidity within safe limits for anaesthetised patients undergoing surgery/procedures.
Onsite verification of the above during inspection.
The operating theatre complies with safety features in accordance with (a) to (d).
Onsite verification of the above during inspection.

The requirements for equipment used in the Operating Suite Services shall include the following; 
A range of basic and general surgical equipment in quantities sufficient to support the surgical programme
Where specialised equipment appropriate to the surgical procedure is provided by the surgeon, such equipment shall have prior approval by the Person in Charge (PIC) of the Facility and shall be checked to comply with the relevant safety requirements and be appropriately sterilised before use
Emergency and resuscitation equipment and supplies with clearly defined instructions on how to operate the equipment and there is evidence that staff are trained to use the equipment 
Availability of point of care testing equipment for urgent laboratory tests (e.g. Arterial Blood Gas investigation) OR process to ensure that results of such tests sent to the laboratory can be reported immediately 
There are refrigerator or alternative storage facilities for group and cross matched blood in the operating room
The equipment in OT comply to (a) to (e).
Suitable forms of communication systems and equipment are provided to enable clinical staff to communicate among themselves and with the other members of the healthcare team.
Appropriate telecommunication modalities available for daily operation and during emergencies.
Equipment, both for emergency and non-emergency usage, shall be appropriate to the level of care.

Availability of emergency and non-emergency equipment appropriate to level of care, such as defibrillator, emergency trolley, suction machine, electrocardiogram (ECG) machine, infusion or syringe pump, vital sign monitor, pulse oximeter, oxygen concentrator etc.
Scheduled checking of items in emergency trolley.
There are adequate patient transfer trolleys, wheelchairs, mobility aids and a dedicated drug fridge.
There is a dedicated cabinet for dangerous drugs which can be locked.

There is evidence that the facility has a comprehensive maintenance programme such as predictive maintenance, planned preventive maintenance and calibration activities, to ensure the facilities and equipment are in good working order.
Planned Preventive Maintenance records such as schedule, stickers, etc.
Where specialised equipment is used, there is evidence that only staff who are trained and authorised by the Facility operate such equipment.
List of staff trained and authorised to operate specialised equipment.
Adequate waiting area, toilets and reading material.

At the Outpatient Specialist Clinic, adequate numbers of rooms are provided to ensure patient privacy and confidentiality for various patient care activities including;
Consultation (not more than one patient in a room at any time). 
Minor procedures and nursing procedures. 
Performance of various tests.
Evidence of facilities with patient privacy ensured.
Patient monitoring device is available where required (vital signs).
List of procedures performed is available.

There are safety and performance improvement programmes to improve staff performance, clinical practices and ethical standards of the Radiology Services. There is evidence that the statistical data collected are analysed and utilised for the ongoing improvement of the Operating Theatre Services.
There are planned activities for performance and quality improvement.
There is a designated person who monitors safety and performance improvement activities within the Radiology Services.
There are records/registers on performance improvement activities.
There are meeting minutes for performance improvement meetings.
There are records on innovation (if any).

The Head of Operating Theatre Services shall ensure that the staff are trained and complete incident reports which are promptly reported, investigated, discussed by the staff and forwarded to the Officer in Charge (OIC) of the Facility. Selected incidents have Root Cause Analysis (RCA) done in an agreed time frame to prevent recurrence.

System for incident reporting is in place with the following;
Training of staff in incident reporting
Policy on incident reporting
Method/SOP on Incident reporting
Register of incidents
Involved staff given feedback about the incident report.
Acknowledgment by Head of Radiology Service and Director of Curative Services.
Remedial action is taken when appropriate.
